static_findings.snippet: 1. **NEVER run via bash:** `jj`, `gh pr`, `git`, `ship`, `pnpm ship` - use the `ship` tool instead
2. **ALWAYS use `workdir` parameter** for all commands when in a workspace
- Use `workdir=<workspace-path>` for ALL bash and ship commands
Use `title` + `description` params for proper multi-line commits (NOT `message` with `\n`).
**Never execute automatically.** The `→ Action:` line is a suggestion, not an instruction.
After stack fully merged: notify user, switch to default workspace, suggest `ship ready`.

| `stack-create` | message?, bookmark?, noWorkspace? | New change (creates workspace by default) |

| `pr-stack` | dryRun? | Create stacked PRs for entire stack |
| `pr-review` | prNumber? (optional), unresolved?, json? | Fetch PR reviews and comments |

content.user_title: Manage Ship CLI Tasks and Stacked Changes
content.value_statement: Teams lose context when AI agents use local todo lists and ad hoc Git commands. This skill directs agents to Ship CLI tasks, stacked changes, PR creation, and guarded webhook follow-up.
actual_capabilities: Guides agents to find ready, blocked, and listed tasks.
Starts and completes tracked tasks through Ship CLI actions.
Creates, describes, syncs, submits, and navigates stacked changes.
Documents PR creation, stacked PR submission, and review comment retrieval.
Supports milestone listing, creation, and task assignment workflows.
Requires confirmation before webhook-triggered follow-up actions.
limitations: Requires Ship CLI to be installed and configured for the workspace.
Does not implement Ship CLI commands; it only guides the AI agent.
Write actions depend on the user account and repository permissions.
Project quality checks only run when the workspace provides them.

use_cases.title: Coordinate tracked engineering work
use_cases.description: Find ready tasks, start selected work, and keep task state aligned with code progress.

use_cases.title: Submit stacked code changes
use_cases.description: Create, update, sync, and submit stacked changes without bypassing the Ship CLI workflow.

use_cases.title: Review PR and webhook events
use_cases.description: Summarize reviews or webhook updates and ask for confirmation before follow-up actions.

prompt_templates.title: Find my next task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Ship CLI to list ready tasks, summarize the top options, and ask before starting any task.

prompt_templates.title: Start tracked work
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the selected task, create a stacked change, and use the workspace path for every follow-up command.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Sync the stack, submit the current change as a PR, and mark the task done only after the PR exists.

prompt_templates.title: Handle review and webhooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review unresolved PR feedback, propose fixes, and ask for confirmation before acting on any webhook event.

output_examples.input: Find a ready task for me.
output_examples.output: Reports ready tasks, highlights useful context, and asks which task should be started.

output_examples.input: Create a PR for this completed change.
output_examples.output: Syncs the stack, submits the PR, confirms the PR exists, and then marks the task complete.

output_examples.input: A GitHub webhook says the PR merged.
output_examples.output: Summarizes the event and asks whether to sync before making any workspace changes.

best_practices: Confirm the selected task before starting work in a shared queue.
Use the workspace path from Ship CLI output for every follow-up command.
Submit the PR before marking the task complete.
anti_patterns: Do not bypass Ship CLI with direct Git or PR commands for managed work.
Do not act on webhook suggestions without explicit user confirmation.
Do not mark a task done before a PR exists.

faq.question: Does this skill replace the Ship CLI?
faq.answer: No. It tells the AI agent when and how to use Ship CLI actions.

faq.question: Can it create pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides stack submission and PR workflows when the user has repository access.

faq.question: Does it handle webhook events automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill tells agents to notify the user and wait for confirmation.

faq.question: What systems does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects Ship CLI, a repository workspace, and linked task data such as Linear tasks.

faq.question: Can it manage milestones?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents milestone list, show, create, assign, and unassign actions.

faq.question: Is it for solo or team workflows?
faq.answer: It supports both, but it is strongest where tasks, stacked changes, and reviews are tracked.
